_about: The BRIEF-2 §4b technique ledger: one row per avenue — how it was tried, its measured effect on which benchmark, kept or dropped, and why. 'Investigated and dropped with a number' is a respectable outcome; a feature bolted on for coverage is not. Numbers are SSE (lower better) unless noted. Baselines are v1's, from output/BASELINES-v2.json.

avenues.how: Short-time complex projection of the residual onto each atom's frequency gives that partial's amplitude track; fit <=8 dB nodes by energy-weighted recursive max-deviation splitting (src/envelope.js); written into amp_env genes with arbitrary node placement. Preserves additivity so the LS gain solve stays exact.
avenues.measured: decay-440 at a 3-wave budget: SSE fell ~10,000x+ vs stationary (one enveloped wave replaces ~48 stationary sines). Speech construct-only: 312.9 -> 258.9. Unit test: >=10x at a 3-wave budget.
avenues.verdict: KEPT — the single biggest win; on by default (ampEnv).

avenues.how: Follow a partial's frequency ridge frame-by-frame (windowed golden refine), fit <=8 cents nodes, write pitch_master + pitch_env (src/pitch-track.js). Per-atom A/B: adopt only if it captures more residual energy than the stationary wave.
avenues.measured: Speech construct-only 258.9 -> 232.4 (11 waves adopted a glide). Ceiling: a fast 2-octave chirp's ridge is recovered correctly (3401 cents) but 8 linear cents nodes cannot hold sample-level phase coherence over 44k samples, so the A/B keeps it stationary there.
avenues.verdict: KEPT — helps speech; self-rejects where it cannot hold phase (honest).

avenues.how: Detect a repeating burst in a partial (fine amplitude track -> autocorrelation for the period -> fold for duty and pre-offset; src/gate-repeat.js). Per-atom A/B builds ONE mid_wait wave for the whole comb, kept only if it beats the incumbent.
avenues.measured: Detector recovers the recover-6wave 426 Hz comb: period 0.318s / duty 0.033 (true 0.317s / 0.023), and correctly rejects the play-once 5.7 Hz wave and continuous tones. recover-6wave overall reached 21.97 (5.96x MIMIC, beats v1 33.29). Burst timing is then snapped to exact integer samples by lockRepeatingGate (src/optimize.js), the analog of lockGate for combs — the single largest reducer of recover-6wave residual.
avenues.verdict: KEPT — recover-6wave key; recover-6wave reached 9.61 (13.6x MIMIC, still descending; SSE=0 exists so this is a search limit, not a ceiling).

avenues.how: INVESTIGATED two ways. (a) v1's report claimed recover-6wave's residual comb came from a 'gated, PM/AM-modulated carrier'; I tested that. (b) I built a synthetic FM target (a 2-slot genome: 400 Hz carrier PM'd by an 80 Hz modulator) to reveal what modulation recovery is actually worth.
avenues.measured: (a) Disabling every pm_on/am_on in the recover-6wave solution changes its render by SSE 0.000 — the target has NO active modulation (every pm_source/am_source points to an inactive slot); its 'comb' is pure gate repetition (avenue 3). (b) On the synthetic FM target (SSE 0 exists as 2 slots), pure additive reaches only SSE 296 at the full 64-wave budget (19.6x silence) — additive genuinely CANNOT compactly reproduce an FM comb. So modulation recovery has real value IN PRINCIPLE, but no benchmark (recover-2/6wave, chimes, speech) contains active modulation.
avenues.verdict: DROPPED from the pipeline — value proven on a synthetic FM target, but measured benefit on all four benchmarks is 0 (none contain modulation). Building an open-ended FM inverse-solver only to pass a synthetic I invented would be 'coverage-gaming' the brief; the honest call is to record the number and not ship complexity the owner must maintain for 0 benchmark gain. The correct mechanism for the real comb (gate repetition) IS built.

avenues.how: INVESTIGATED alongside avenue 4 — the same FM synthetic uses a modulator slot (gain_out_on off, gain_mod_on on) as a free operator, exactly this avenue's mechanism.
avenues.measured: The 2-slot operator pair renders the FM comb at SSE 0; additive needs all 64 slots and still sits at SSE 296. So one operator + one carrier does what 64 additive waves cannot — the capability is real and large where a target is FM-generated.
avenues.verdict: DROPPED for the benchmarks (same reason as avenue 4: no benchmark is FM-generated). The mixer marks any modulator wave and its PM/AM edges honestly, so if a future target's genome uses operators, the artifact shows them as what they are.

avenues.how: INVESTIGATED. Built a target that is ONE wave with mixed shapes (0.6 sine + 0.4 triangle, both on) and asked how additive single-shape-per-wave construction copes.
avenues.measured: Additive reaches SSE 8.5 with 1 wave, 1.36 with 2, 0.19 with 4 — i.e. separate single-shape waves at the same frequency already SPAN the mixed-shape space and converge quickly; a mixed-shape wave would nail it in one slot. So mixed shapes buy SLOT EFFICIENCY, not new SSE reach.
avenues.verdict: DROPPED from the pipeline — redundant with the additive LS (which already spans weighted shape sums via separate waves) for SSE; it only saves slots, and once amplitude envelopes freed slots the 64-slot budget was not the binding constraint on the benchmarks. Recorded, not integrated.

avenues.how: In the scheduler (src/schedule.js): rank active waves by marginal SSE contribution, kill the least useful, re-spend its slot on the largest unexplained residual via the shared fitOneAtom, LS re-solve, keep only if SSE drops.
avenues.measured: Speech 2.5-min run: reallocation fired (realloc+4 in epoch 1) as part of 232.4 -> 209.85. The one structural move coordinate descent cannot make (hopping a wave across a spectral valley).
avenues.verdict: KEPT — part of every budgeted run.

avenues.how: Independent multi-start (src/pool.js): --workers runs N complete construct+schedule pipelines (different seeds) as child processes sharing the budget; keep the best. Capped at 4 for compute courtesy. Coordinate descent (the dominant move) is sequential, so multi-start is the effective core->quality conversion; CMA-ES-population parallelism was considered but gives less here.
avenues.measured: Verified end-to-end: `--workers 2` on recover-6wave spawned two seed-diverged child pipelines to separate dirs, picked the lower-SSE one, copied it to the run dir, and verify.js PASSED. A clean workers=4-vs-1 equal-wall-clock speedup number was not taken because this container heavily contends (and hides/won’t-kill background procs), which would make the comparison noise; the mechanism and its correctness are confirmed, the quantified speedup is left for the owner’s machine (noted in report §10).
